mainTopic: מגילת תענית after the חורבן, the messengers announcing the new month, and the lengths of the אדר months
overview: The amud opens by finishing a source that showed the days of מגילת תענית still being kept after the חורבן. The גמרא explains that this is a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי. It concludes that חנוכה and פורים were never cancelled, while the other days were. Next it returns to the משנה about messengers. They are sent in תשרי as well as אלול because אלול can be given an extra day when needed. In that case it is better to lose ראש השנה than all the later holidays. The גמרא then notes that our משנה sends no messengers for אדר שני, unlike רבי. It explains this as a dispute over whether the added leap month has a fixed length. Several traditions follow about how long the two אדרים are, including a ruling that the אדר before ניסן is always short. רב נחמן begins to challenge that ruling from a משנה about breaking שבת for ניסן, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the earlier source
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a source quoted just before this point: the חכמים rule that the item is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a source the גמרא started quoting just before this section. That source was used to show that מגילת תענית was still in force even after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source involved a time after the בית המקדש was destroyed. It suggested that the days of מגילת תענית were still being kept then. That raises a problem for anyone who says מגילת תענית was cancelled, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, meaning the majority opinion
Declare it pure
An ancient list of happy days on which fasting was not allowed

phrases.english: And the Sages declare it pure.
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of a source the גמרא quoted just before this section begins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מגילת תענית was cancelled after the חורבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier source shows the days of מגילת תענית still being kept after the חורבן.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question is a dispute between תנאים. It brings a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says the days stay forbidden for fasting forever, and רבי יוסי says they are permitted once the בית המקדש is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches. רבי מאיר says that the days written in מגילת תענית are forbidden for fasting, whether or not the בית המקדש is standing. רבי יוסי says that when the בית המקדש stands they are forbidden, because they are days of joy. When it is not standing they are permitted, because they are days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that this question is a disagreement between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא to show both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source from step 1 fits רבי מאיר, who holds the days were never cancelled. The view that they were cancelled follows רבי יוסי. For רבי יוסי, the joy of these days depended on the בית המקדש, so once it was destroyed the reason to celebrate them was gone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The Temple is standing
Forbidden or permitted (here, for fasting)
Mourning

steps.confusionAlert: Here "forbidden" means forbidden to fast. These days were happy days, so fasting on them was not allowed.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it is taught in a baraita:
These days which are written in Megillat Ta'anit,
whether at a time when the Temple is standing

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים —
phrases.english: or at a time when the Temple is not standing,
are forbidden; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Forbidden for fasting, since these are celebration days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים — אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: When the Temple is standing, they are forbidden,
because it is a joy for them.
When the Temple is not standing, they are permitted,
because it is mourning for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing that the issue is a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees about whether מגילת תענית was cancelled, so the earlier source is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier source follows רבי מאיר. The view that it was cancelled follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Two rulings that seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports two rulings: the days were cancelled, and the days were not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is that they were cancelled, and the הלכה is that they were not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states two practical rulings that seem to say opposite things. This sets up the next step, which points out the clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ruling matches רבי יוסי (the days were cancelled). The other matches רבי מאיר (the days were not cancelled). Both are given as הלכה, so a problem is about to come up.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה (the practical ruling) is
They were cancelled

phrases.english: And the halakha is: they were nullified,
and the halakha is: they were not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical rulings on the dispute from step 2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are said to be הלכה, which still needs to be explained.

steps.title: The two rulings contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one ruling contradicts the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: One הלכה contradicts the other הלכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how both rulings can be true, since they say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the days were cancelled, they cannot also be not cancelled. The challenge forces the גמרא to show that each ruling covers different days.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (a contradiction)
One ruling against the other ruling

phrases.english: One halakha is difficult against the other halakha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two rulings in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opposite rulings cannot both apply to the same thing.

steps.title: חנוכה and פורים stayed; the other days were cancelled
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. חנוכה and פורים were not cancelled, while the rest of the days in מגילת תענית were.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the ruling is about חנוכה and פורים. There, it is about the rest of the days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying each ruling is about different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling "not cancelled" is about חנוכה and פורים, which are still kept. The ruling "cancelled" is about all the other days listed in מגילת תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
Here... there (each ruling is about a different case)
The rest of the days

steps.whatToRemember: מגילת תענית was cancelled after the חורבן, except for חנוכה and פורים, which are still kept.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why חנוכה and פורים keep their status from מגילת תענית today, such as the ban on fasting, while the other days in מגילת תענית are no longer observed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about Hanukkah and Purim,
phrases.notes: This goes with the ruling "they were not nullified."

phrases.english: there, it is about the rest of the days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ruling is about different cases (כאן... כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings are about all the days of מגילת תענית.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנוכה and פורים were not cancelled. All the other days were.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: messengers in אלול and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: messengers go out in אלול because of ראש השנה, and in תשרי to set the dates of the holidays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: messengers go out for אלול because of ראש השנה, and for תשרי to set the holidays correctly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the next line. This sets up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The announcement for אלול tells people when ראש השנה falls. The announcement for תשרי tells them when the holidays of that month fall.

keyTerms.meaning: The month before ראש השנה
The month of ראש השנה, סוכות and other holidays
Setting the holidays on the correct dates

phrases.english: For Elul, because of Rosh HaShana,
and for Tishrei, because of setting the Festivals correctly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Messengers go out in אלול for ראש השנה and in תשרי for the holidays.

steps.title: Why do they need to go out in תשרי too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: once the messengers went out for אלול, why do they need to go out again for תשרי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they already went out for אלול, why do they need to go out for תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה and asks why a second trip is needed. Step 8 blocks one possible answer, and step 9 gives the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that once people know when אלול began, they can count forward and know when תשרי begins. If so, the trip for תשרי seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, once
They went out
Why do they need it?

phrases.english: Since they already went out for Elul,
why do they need to go out for Tishrei?
phrases.notes: The idea is that once people know when אלול started, they can count ahead to know when תשרי starts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of messengers for תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The date of תשרי can already be worked out from the announcement for אלול, so a second trip seems unneeded.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that אלול might have an extra day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers answering that אלול may have been given an extra day, which would explain the תשרי messengers. It rejects this using רב's statement that since עזרא, אלול never had an extra day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that perhaps they added a day to אלול, that would explain the messengers in תשרי. But didn't רבי חיננא בר כהנא say in the name of רב: From the days of עזרא onward, we never found an אלול with an extra day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer to its question from step 7 and immediately knocks it down. The question stays strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלול might have 30 days, people would need a second message to know when ראש חודש תשרי really was. But רב says אלול has always had only 29 days since עזרא's time. So everyone can count the תשרי dates from the אלול message, and the second set of messengers still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a possible answer, often to reject it)
They added a day to it (made the month 30 days long)
Given an extra day; a full 30-day month
From the days of עזרא and onward
We have not found; it never happened

steps.confusionAlert: Here מעובר means a month with an extra 30th day. It does not mean adding a whole extra month to the year.

phrases.english: And if you say: perhaps they added a day to Elul,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Kahana say that Rav said:
From the days of Ezra and onward
we have not found an Elul with an extra day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דִּלְמָא עַבְּרוּהּ לֶאֱלוּל, וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question of step 7 by blocking an obvious answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the תשרי messengers are needed because אלול may have had an extra day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב testifies that אלול has never had an extra day since עזרא, so its length is always known.

steps.title: It never happened only because it was never needed
steps.stepSummary: רב's statement only means it was never needed. If it is needed, a day is added to אלול, so the תשרי messengers are still necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We have not found' means it was never needed. But if it is needed, we do add a day to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב's statement more carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was describing what has happened, not setting a rule that it can never happen. Since בית דין could still add a day to אלול, nobody can be sure when ראש חודש תשרי fell. That is why messengers must go out in תשרי too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
We add a day to it

phrases.english: 'We have not found' means that it was not needed;
but if it were needed, we would add a day to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by limiting what רב's statement means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the cited statement as describing what happened, not what is allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב meant that אלול can never be given an extra day.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלול can get an extra day when needed; it simply never was needed.

steps.title: But then ראש השנה would be ruined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if אלול gets an extra day, distant people will keep ראש השנה on the wrong day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then ראש השנה is ruined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 9 by pointing to a problem it creates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תשרי messengers leave only after ראש השנה, so distant communities cannot hear about the extra day in time. They will count 30 days from ראש חודש אלול and keep ראש השנה a day too early. How could בית דין allow that?

keyTerms.meaning: Is ruined; goes wrong

phrases.english: But then Rosh HaShana is ruined!
phrases.notes: People far away would keep ראש השנה a day early, because they don't know אלול got an extra day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית דין may add a day to אלול when needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding a day to אלול makes distant communities keep ראש השנה on the wrong day.

steps.title: Better to lose ראש השנה than all the holidays
steps.stepSummary: It is better for ראש השנה to be ruined than for all the מועדים of תשרי to be ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Better that ראש השנה be ruined, and not all the holidays be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that ראש השנה may be affected and explains why that is the better choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When needed, בית דין adds the day even though ראש השנה will go wrong for distant people. That way the תשרי messengers can still give everyone the right dates for יום כיפור, סוכות and שמיני עצרת. Losing one day is better than losing all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is better
The holidays

phrases.english: Better that Rosh HaShana be ruined
and not have all the holidays be ruined.
phrases.notes: He means the holidays later in תשרי: יום כיפור, סוכות and שמיני עצרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the problem and explains why it is the smaller loss.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since adding a day to אלול would ruin ראש השנה, it should never be done.
steps.terutzMaskana: When needed, the day is added, because protecting all the מועדים matters more than ראש השנה alone.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports this
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the תשרי messengers go out 'to set the dates of the holidays', which fits this explanation. The גמרא concludes it is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, since it teaches: 'For תשרי, to set the dates of the holidays.' Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the משנה's own words and then closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say the תשרי messengers go out for ראש השנה. It says they go out for the holidays. This matches the answer that ראש השנה may be lost, while the תשרי messengers protect the later holidays.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it supports this)
Setting the holidays on the correct dates
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: Messengers go out in תשרי because אלול can get an extra day when needed. Then ראש השנה may be lost for distant people, but the later holidays are saved. The משנה's words 'מפני תקנת המועדות' show this.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact, as it teaches:
'In Tishrei, to set the dates of the holidays.'
phrases.notes: This is the משנה quoted in step 6. Notice it mentions the holidays, not ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it is so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 11 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the תשרי messengers exist to protect the holidays, even if ראש השנה is lost.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'על תשרי מפני תקנת המועדות'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תשרי messengers are needed for the holidays after ראש השנה, since אלול may get an extra day.

steps.title: The משנה leaves out אדר שני, so it does not follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's mention of כסלו and אדר. It notes that the משנה never says messengers go out for אדר שני in a leap year, so the משנה must disagree with רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says messengers go out in כסלו because of חנוכה and in אדר because of פורים. But it does not say that in a leap year they also go out in אדר שני because of פורים. So our משנה does not follow רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and notices something missing: nothing about a second אדר. From that silence it concludes that the משנה is not like רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an inference from what the משנה does not say. If messengers went out for אדר שני, the משנה should have listed it. Since it did not, the משנה must hold that no messengers are sent for אדר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of כסלו, when חנוכה falls
The year was made a leap year, with an extra אדר added
The second אדר, added in a leap year; פורים is kept in it
It does not teach it; the משנה leaves it out
Our משנה

phrases.english: And in Kislev, because of Chanukah,
and in Adar, because of Purim.
But 'if the year was made a leap year,
they go out also for the second Adar
because of Purim' is not taught.
Our Mishnah is not like Rebbi.
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תשרי messengers to the next months in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the משנה does not mention messengers for אדר שני, it does not follow רבי.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי says messengers go out for אדר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי holds messengers go out for אדר שני in a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי says that if the year was made a leap year, messengers go out also for אדר שני because of פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for רבי's opinion, which proves the משנה really disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact wording the משנה left out. That shows the missing line was a real opinion that someone held, and our משנה chose not to follow it.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rebbi says:
If the year was made a leap year,
they go out also for the second Adar
because of Purim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי's opinion mentioned in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה disagrees with רבי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי that messengers go out for אדר שני

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue about doing אדר שני's מצוות in אדר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה holds מצוות of אדר שני count if done in אדר ראשון, so no messengers are needed, while רבי holds they do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is what they argue about? One side, the משנה, holds that all the מצוות kept in אדר שני can also be kept in אדר ראשון. The other side, רבי, holds that מצוות kept in אדר שני cannot be kept in אדר ראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason behind the argument. It is only a suggestion, and the גמרא will test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If keeping פורים in אדר ראשון counts, it does not matter if people far away miss the date of אדר שני, so no messengers are needed. If it does not count, people must know exactly when אדר שני is, so messengers must be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion
They argue
מצוות that are kept in אדר שני, like פורים
In the first אדר

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַנּוֹהֲגוֹת בַּשֵּׁנִי —
phrases.english: that one master holds: all מצוות kept in the second [Adar]
phrases.notes: 'One master' is the author of our משנה.

phrases.english: may be kept in the first,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַנּוֹהֲגוֹת בַּשֵּׁנִי —
phrases.english: and the other master holds: all מצוות kept in the second
may not be kept in the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the reason behind the argument found in steps 13-14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying reason for the argument between the משנה and רבי?

steps.title: No: everyone agrees, and they argue about the length of the leap month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees that אדר שני's מצוות cannot be done in אדר ראשון. The real argument is about the added leap-year month.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that מצוות kept in אדר שני cannot be kept in אדר ראשון. Here they argue about the leap-year addition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from step 15 and points to a different reason for the argument. The next step brings the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides agree that people must keep פורים in the right אדר. The argument moves to a factual question: can people work out on their own when אדר שני falls? That depends on how long the added month is.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Making the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees:
מצוות kept in the second [Adar]
may not be kept in the first,
and here they argue about the leap-year addition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation offered in step 15 and replaces it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested reason for the argument, not the argument itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument does not need to depend on whether אדר שני's מצוות can be done in אדר ראשון; there is a better explanation.

steps.title: The ברייתא: is the added month thirty days or 'a month'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows an argument: the תנא קמא says the leap addition is thirty days, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is 'a month'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: How long is the leap-year addition? Thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind its new explanation. Our משנה follows the thirty-day view, and רבי follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the added month is always thirty days, people can count by themselves and know when אדר שני and its פורים fall, so no messengers are needed. If it is 'a month' whose length is not fixed, people cannot know, so messengers must go out, as רבי says.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirty days, a fixed length
'A month', which may not be a fixed length

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כַּמָּה עִיבּוּר שָׁנָה — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: As it was taught: How much is the leap-year addition? Thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the argument about the leap-year addition introduced in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה and רבי argue about the length of the added month
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the תנא קמא says thirty days and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a month

steps.title: But people can count 'a month' too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if thirty days is known, 'a month' should be known too, because a plain month means twenty-nine days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are thirty days different? Because people know them? People know 'a month' too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from steps 16-17. It argues that 'a month' is also a fixed length, so there should be no need for messengers under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation only works if 'a month' has an unknown length. If 'a month' simply means twenty-nine days, people can count it just as easily as thirty, and the difference between the two opinions disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
They know

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree a month is added. The question is only whether its length is fixed so people can count it, not whether a month is added at all.

phrases.english: What is different about thirty? That people know [its length]?
A month, they also know!
phrases.notes: He means a plain 'month' is twenty-nine days, so people could count that too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation built in steps 16-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'a month' leaves people unsure when אדר שני falls
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A month is also a known length (twenty-nine days), so people could count it without messengers.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'a month' lets the court choose either length
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the view of 'a month' lets the court pick twenty-nine or thirty days, so people cannot know the length and messengers are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The one who says 'a month' means that if the court wants, it adds a month of twenty-nine days, and if it wants, it adds thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining what 'a month' really means. This saves the explanation that the argument is about the length of the added month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל the length is up to the court, so distant people cannot work out the date of פורים, and רבי sends messengers. Under the thirty-day view the length is always the same, so the משנה needs no messengers for אדר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: If it wants; here, if the court chooses

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (thirty fixed days) sends no messengers for אדר שני because people can count. רבי follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, where the court may choose twenty-nine or thirty days, so messengers must tell people when פורים is.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The one who says 'a month' [means]:
if it wants, a month; if it wants, thirty.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the court, and 'a month' here means a short month of twenty-nine days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאן דְּאָמַר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the term 'a month' in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A month' means a fixed twenty-nine days, which people can count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'A month' means the court may choose twenty-nine or thirty days, so the length cannot be known without messengers.

steps.title: Both אדרים are declared on the thirtieth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי testifies, in the name of the holy community of ירושלים, that both אדר months are made short. The next month always begins on the thirtieth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי testified in the name of the holy community of ירושלים that the new month after each of the two אדרים is declared on the thirtieth day. That is the day that could have made the month full.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought about the two אדר months of a leap year. They are always ended after 29 days, and the next month starts on day thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month is either 'short' (29 days) or 'full' (30 days). Here the thirtieth day becomes the new ראש חודש instead of being added to אדר. So both אדר ראשון and אדר שני are always 29 days.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified; formally reported a received tradition
The holy community of Jerusalem, a respected group of sages
The two months of אדר in a leap year
Their 'day of extension': the thirtieth day, which could have made the month full

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi testified
in the name of the holy community of Jerusalem
about the two Adars
that they are sanctified on their day of extension.
phrases.notes: The thirtieth day, which could have made אדר full, is made ראש חודש instead, so each אדר has only 29 days.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of month lengths from steps 18-19 with a new tradition about the two אדר months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אדר months are made short. The following month is always sanctified on the thirtieth day.

steps.title: This testimony excludes a different tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out what the testimony means: the אדר months are made short, never full. It says this rejects what רב נחמן בר חסדא taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is to say, we make them short and we do not make them full! This comes to exclude what רב נחמן בר חסדא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the plain meaning out of רבי יהושע בן לוי's testimony. It then sets up the opposing tradition, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the thirtieth day is always ראש חודש, then neither אדר can ever be full. That clashes with the tradition of רב נחמן בר חסדא, which allows full months. The testimony is meant to push that tradition aside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is to say': drawing out what a statement implies
Short months of 29 days
Full months of 30 days
'To exclude': this comes to reject another view

phrases.english: That is to say that we make them short
but we do not make them full!

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּדָרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: This is to exclude what Rav Nachman bar Chisda taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 20 implies and names the view it rejects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the אדר months are only made short, against רב נחמן בר חסדא's tradition.

steps.title: The court may make the אדרים full or short
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר חסדא's tradition: רבי סימאי testified in the name of the prophets חגי, זכריה and מלאכי that the court may make the two אדר months both full, both short, or one of each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימאי testified in the name of חגי, זכריה and מלאכי about the two אדרים. If the court wants to make both full, it may. If it wants both short, it may. If it wants one full and one short, it may. And this is how they acted in the גולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the tradition that step 21 said was being rejected. This tradition gives the court full freedom over the length of both אדר months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of step 20. There, both months are always short. Here, any combination is allowed, so people far away cannot be sure how long each אדר was.

keyTerms.meaning: The last prophets of the Second Temple period
'They may do so': the court is allowed to choose this
The Diaspora, Jews living outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Simai testified
in the name of Chaggai, Zechariah, and Malachi
about two Adars,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצוּ לַעֲשׂוֹתָן שְׁנֵיהֶן מְלֵאִין — עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: that if they wanted to make both of them full, they do so;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the court that sets the calendar.

phrases.english: both of them short, they do so;
one full and one short, they do so.
And this is how they would act in the Diaspora.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי סִימַאי מִשּׁוּם חַגַּי זְכַרְיָה וּמַלְאָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the opposing tradition that step 21 said was being rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court may set the two אדר months as both full, both short, or one full and one short.

steps.title: רב: assume one full and one short
steps.stepSummary: In רב's name they said that people should always treat the two אדרים as one full and one short. The exception is when they know ראש חודש was set at its normal time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the name of our teacher they said: Always treat them as one full and one short, unless you find out that ראש חודש was set at its time.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion is added, giving a working rule for people who do not know what the court decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people far away cannot know how the court set the months, רב gives a default: one full and one short. If they learn that ראש חודש came at its expected time, they follow that information instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our teacher': here it means רב
Until it becomes known to you, meaning unless you find out
At its normal, expected time

phrases.english: And in the name of our teacher they said:
always one full and one short,
unless it becomes known to you
that Rosh Chodesh was fixed at its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical default rule for when the court's choice is unknown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By default, the two אדר months are treated as one full and one short, unless you know ראש חודש came at its time.

steps.title: The אדר before ניסן is always short
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent from ארץ ישראל to מר עוקבא: the אדר right before ניסן is always short.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to מר עוקבא: The אדר next to ניסן is always short.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling is brought, a message sent to מר עוקבא in בבל. It fixes the length of the אדר that comes right before ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling only fixes the אדר next to ניסן. In a regular year that is the only אדר, and in a leap year it is אדר שני. It says nothing fixed about אדר ראשון, which can be full at times.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They sent to him': a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל
The אדר right before ניסן

phrases.english: They sent to Mar Ukva:
The Adar that is next to Nisan
is always short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ruling about אדר's length, focused only on the אדר next to ניסן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אדר immediately before ניסן is always 29 days.

steps.title: Why break שבת for ניסן if אדר is fixed?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges the ruling sent to מר עוקבא. A משנה says witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon of ניסן. That only makes sense if אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: The משנה says witnesses may break שבת for two months, ניסן and תשרי. It makes sense if you say אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short. Because of that, they break שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts a challenge against step 24 using a משנה. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are only needed if their testimony can change the date. If אדר can be 29 or 30 days, testimony on day thirty decides when ניסן starts, so breaking שבת makes sense. If אדר were always short, the date would be known ahead of time, and breaking שבת would seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: They break שבת (to travel and testify)
'It works well if you say': setting up a contrast before the challenge
Sometimes

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished yet. רב נחמן has only said the side that works, 'if אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short'. The 'but if it is always short' part comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman objected:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: For two months they break Shabbos,
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who saw the new moon, traveling on שבת to testify.

phrases.english: for Nisan and for Tishrei.
It works well if you say
that it is sometimes full and sometimes short,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the אדר right before ניסן.

phrases.english: because of that we break Shabbos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 24 that the אדר before ניסן is always short.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling sent to מר עוקבא that the אדר next to ניסן is always short.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows breaking שבת to testify about ניסן's new moon. That makes sense only if the testimony can decide whether אדר is 29 or 30 days. If אדר were always short, the testimony would change nothing.
